as.bilingual_pair_policy: This Nigeria Primary 1-3 Mathematics curriculum is English-only. Do not create bilingual pairs, translations, or cross-language duplicate candidates. Preserve visible English source text exactly. If non-English text appears incidentally, keep it only as source-visible text and do not translate it or pair it with an English candidate unless the document itself explicitly presents both versions as equivalent official curriculum text.

as.sfi_dedup_instructions: Deduplicate Nigeria Primary 1-3 Mathematics SFI candidates conservatively. Merge candidates only when they represent the same source-visible curriculum item in the same grade/theme/sub-theme/topic scope. This curriculum does not use stable official alphanumeric statement codes for the SFI hierarchy. Do not treat visible topic row numbers, list numbers, roman numerals, bullet numbers, page numbers, examples, or table row ordinals as globally meaningful statement codes or as merge keys. Preserve a Topic's visible leading row ordinal as part of its source-facing Topic description. Within the same Grade, Theme, and Sub-Theme, different ordinals on otherwise repeated Topic labels identify different source Topic occurrences unless the evidence shows duplicate extraction of the same row. The ordinal remains a local occurrence discriminator only, never a statement code or cross-grade merge key. Repeated Grade headings such as PRIMARY ONE, PRIMARY TWO, PRIMARY THREE, and source/OCR punctuation variants such as PRIMARY: THREE should be merged by grade when the visible text and source references indicate the same grade organizer. Repeated Theme and Sub-Theme headings should be merged only within the same grade and curriculum scope; do not merge a repeated Theme/Sub-Theme label across different grades unless the bounded evidence clearly shows duplicate extraction of the same source-visible organizer rather than distinct grade-scoped organizers. Topic labels such as Whole Numbers, Addition, Subtraction, Multiplication, Division, Open Sentences, Money, Length, Time, Weight, Capacity, Area, Data Collection, Fractions, Symmetry, Pictograms, or Shapes recur across grades and sometimes within the same grade; keep them separate unless the source references, grade, theme, sub-theme, and row/table context identify the same topic instance. Performance Objective candidates are often repeated or similar across topics and grades; merge them only when they are duplicate extractions of the same objective occurrence, adjacent-window overlap, or a clear continuation duplicate. Content, Activities, Teacher/Pupils activities, teaching and learning resources/materials, and evaluation guide text are not SFIs and should not appear as registry candidates or drive merges except as source-context evidence. Same source row/header overlap, same source segment, same window proximity, duplicate buckets, and same normalized text buckets are review signals only, not automatic merge rules. When evidence is insufficient to distinguish repeated no-code labels or similar learning statements, choose keep_separate or needs_review rather than over-merging. For Nigeria heading scope, use each candidate's validated identity_scope_values as the primary semantic scope. When compact source context must be consulted, resolve each scope dimension independently. A Grade remains active across pages until a newer Grade heading supersedes it; a newly visible Theme or Sub-Theme supersedes older entries only for that same statement type. Do not associate a candidate with an older Grade merely because the same Theme or Sub-Theme wording previously appeared under that Grade. Paired visual headers such as 'THEME: X SUB-THEME: Y' identify the local Theme/Sub-Theme pair when source layout supports that reading. Normalize singular/plural header variants such as Primary Measure/Primary Measures and Secondary Measure/Secondary Measures. When candidate scope conflicts with the nearest source-supported Grade and the bounded evidence is insufficient to resolve the conflict, choose needs_review rather than merging across Grades.
as.sfi_extraction_instructions: Extract candidate StandardsFrameworkItems (SFIs) from the Nigeria Primary 1-3 Mathematics curriculum only when the visible text is an official curriculum framework item, structural organizer, or expected learning outcome. The document is organized by Grade/Class labels (PRIMARY ONE, PRIMARY TWO, PRIMARY THREE), Theme, Sub-Theme, Topic, Performance Objectives, and Content. Treat visible PRIMARY ONE, PRIMARY TWO, PRIMARY THREE, and source/OCR punctuation variants such as PRIMARY: THREE labels as Grade Standard Grouping SFIs. Treat visible THEME labels such as NUMBER AND NUMERATION, BASIC OPERATIONS, ALGEBRAIC PROCESSES, MENSURATION AND GEOMETRY, and EVERY DAY STATISTICS as Theme Standard Grouping SFIs. Treat visible SUB-THEME/SUBTHEME labels such as Whole Number, Fraction, Basic Operations, Algebraic Operations, Open Sentences, Primary Measures, Secondary Measure(s), Shapes, and Data Collection and Presentation as Sub-Theme Standard Grouping SFIs. For heading-block Theme and Sub-Theme SFIs, include the complete visible labeled field in description, including THEME, SUB-THEME or SUBTHEME, the colon, source-visible spacing, capitalization, and punctuation. For example, preserve 'THEME: NUMBER AND NUMERATION' and 'SUB-THEME: Whole Number' as the candidate descriptions rather than shortening them to 'NUMBER AND NUMERATION' and 'Whole Number'. Controlled values and aliases are for later recognition, canonicalization, deduplication, and hierarchy resolution only; they must not replace or shorten the source-visible candidate description. Treat visible Topic-column items such as 'Whole numbers 1-5', 'Whole number 0 (Zero)', 'Whole numbers 6-9', 'Whole number 10', 'Whole Numbers 1-99', 'Whole numbers 1-200', 'Whole numbers up to 999', 'Fractions', 'Addition', 'Subtraction', 'Multiplication', 'Division', 'Open Sentences', 'Money', 'Length', 'Length II', 'Capacity', 'Area', 'Time', 'Weight', 'Three dimensional shapes', 'Two dimensional shapes', 'Symmetry', 'Data Collection', and 'Pictograms' as Topic Standard Grouping SFIs. Preserve the complete visible Topic cell in description and source_text, including the leading local Arabic ordinal and punctuation, such as '1. Addition', '3. Addition', '1. Money', or '3. Length II'. The ordinal is source-facing occurrence material used with Grade, Theme, and Sub-Theme to distinguish repeated Topic labels within the same local curriculum scope; it is not an official statement code and must never be placed in statement_code. Treat each numbered item under PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES / Performance Objectives as a Performance Objective Standard SFI. A shared visible stem such as 'Pupils should be able to:', 'Pupil should be able to:', 'The pupils should be able to:', or 'The pupil should be able to:' semantically scopes every top-level objective in that same Performance Objectives cell. When the stem is needed for a complete normative statement, include the exact visible stem together with the exact objective wording in candidate description. For the first objective, source_text may include the stem and objective when they form one contiguous source-visible excerpt. For later objectives, or whenever earlier peer objectives intervene between the shared stem and the current objective, source_text must quote only the exact contiguous current objective item; do not include earlier objectives, do not reconstruct a noncontiguous quote, and do not omit the stem from description when it is needed for completeness. In this case it is valid for description to be assembled from the exact visible stem plus the exact visible objective from the same cited table row while source_text is the contiguous objective excerpt. Treat the visible CONTENT / Content column as official curriculum elaboration and semantic context for its Topic and Performance Objectives, but do not emit Content SFIs in this v0 graph. Do not use Content wording as a Performance Objective description or source anchor unless the same wording is also visible in the Performance Objectives cell. Do not extract LearningComponents in this step and do not decompose a Performance Objective into smaller skills beyond the source-visible top-level objective item. Do not extract Content, Activities, Teacher activities, Pupils activities, Teaching and Learning Resources/Materials, Evaluation Guide items, examples beginning with e.g., classroom procedures, resources, materials, assessment prompts, teacher guidance, or pupil tasks as SFIs. Return such text only as auxiliary when it is unusually prominent or ambiguous. Repeated table headers and repeated continuation labels are not SFIs. Preserve source-language wording exactly. This curriculum has no stable official SFI codes; set statement_code to null unless a future source window contains an explicitly official curriculum code. Do not use topic numbers, roman numerals, list numbers, page numbers, example numbers, clock/money values, or arithmetic expressions as statement_code. For Nigeria identity-scope resolution, resolve every configured scope dimension independently. Do not infer one scope dimension by searching for an older historical combination of Grade, Theme, Sub-Theme, Topic, or another grouping. For each required dimension, first use a controlled value explicitly visible in the current target block or table when the target itself states that dimension. Next apply clear bounded same-page heading context when the page layout establishes a visual reading-order inversion. Otherwise use the nearest recognized candidate for that exact scope statement type in source_context.scope_context_candidates; if no recognized candidate is available, use the first matching entry in source_context.section_path_recent_first. Do not skip a nearer compatible scope value for an older one merely because the older value previously appeared beside the same Theme, Sub-Theme, Topic, or other repeated label. A Grade heading remains active across subsequent pages, tables, and organizer sections until a newer Grade heading supersedes it. Do not reject the nearest Grade merely because its source page precedes the current target page. A newly visible Theme supersedes older Theme entries, and a newly visible Sub-Theme supersedes older Sub-Theme entries, but neither supersedes or invalidates the active Grade. Paired visual headers such as 'THEME: X SUB-THEME: Y' should be interpreted as the active local Theme/Sub-Theme pair for that page or table section. Normalize singular/plural header variants such as Primary Measure/Primary Measures and Secondary Measure/Secondary Measures. On a grade-opening page, a visible Grade heading may follow the current Theme or Sub-Theme block in DocumentIR order even though the page layout shows that it governs those organizers. When bounded same-page heading context clearly establishes that relationship, use that local Grade instead of a stale carried Grade. Inspect preceding and following same-page headings together; do not assume that every following heading governs the target. All source_context content is context-only: never emit or anchor a candidate from it, and do not claim that a page, heading, context direction, source text, or controlled value was supplied unless it is actually present in the compact source window.
as.sfi_extraction_validation_instructions:
Validate Nigeria Primary 1-3 Mathematics SFI extraction as a strict curriculum-specific checker. Apply the generic checker rules and the runtime sfi_extraction_instructions, then use the following source-specific rules to identify material omissions, false positives, wrong splits, wrong statement types, and incorrect source roles.

SOURCE STRUCTURE AND ALLOWED SFI ROLES
- The source is a Primary One, Primary Two, and Primary Three mathematics curriculum presented almost entirely as repeated landscape tables. The only valid SFI statement_type values are Grade, Theme, Sub-Theme, Topic, and Performance Objective.
- Grade, Theme, Sub-Theme, and Topic are Standard Grouping SFIs. Performance Objective is the only Standard SFI type in this v0 graph.
- MATHEMATICS CURRICULUM is the framework title, not an SFI. Table column labels such as TOPIC, PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES, CONTENT, ACTIVITIES, TEACHER, PUPILS, TEACHING AND LEARNING RESOURCES or MATERIALS, and EVALUATION GUIDE are structural headers, not SFIs.
- For table-derived candidates, the source column is decisive. Only visible Topic and Performance Objectives cells may produce table-row SFI candidates. Content is semantic context only. Do not accept candidates extracted from Content, Teacher Activities, Pupils Activities, Teaching and Learning Resources or Materials, or Evaluation Guide, even when those cells repeat or closely paraphrase the performance objectives.

CROSS-TYPE DUPLICATE PREVENTION
- Do not allow one exact source occurrence to survive twice under different statement_type values. When two draft candidates quote the same source span or the same exact allowed table cell/list item and differ only in classification, retain exactly one candidate and assign the type from the source role: Topic-column text is Topic and Performance Objectives-column text is Performance Objective. Content-column text must not survive as an SFI candidate.
- Treat a cross-type duplicate of the same source occurrence as a material error. Set passed=false and return a complete corrected result rather than leaving the duplicate for downstream deduplication. Distinct source-visible items in the same row remain separate even when their wording is similar.

HEADING BLOCKS
- A visible PRIMARY ONE, PRIMARY TWO, PRIMARY THREE, or PRIMARY: THREE heading should produce one Grade candidate. Preserve the visible surface wording; the punctuation variant PRIMARY: THREE is not an error.
- A block containing both a THEME label and a SUB-THEME or SUBTHEME label should normally produce two candidates in source order: one Theme and one Sub-Theme. Do not combine the two lines into one candidate.
- For every Theme and Sub-Theme candidate, the visible hierarchy label and its punctuation are part of the complete official grouping wording and must remain in description. A block containing 'THEME: NUMBER AND NUMERATION' and 'SUB-THEME: Whole Number' must produce descriptions exactly matching 'THEME: NUMBER AND NUMERATION' and 'SUB-THEME: Whole Number', not 'NUMBER AND NUMERATION' and 'Whole Number'. Preserve source-visible variants such as 'THEME :', 'SUB-THEME:', and 'SUBTHEME:' exactly, including spacing, capitalization, and punctuation.
- Controlled values and aliases are for later recognition, canonicalization, deduplication, and hierarchy resolution only. They must never replace or shorten the source-visible Theme or Sub-Theme description.
- Omitting THEME, SUB-THEME, or SUBTHEME from a visible heading description is a material source-fidelity error. Set passed=false and return a corrected result.
- Do not add a Grade, Theme, or Sub-Theme candidate solely because it appears in source_context.section_path_recent_first or elsewhere on the same page. It must be visible in the current block or table source content.
- Validate every configured identity-scope dimension independently. For each required dimension, identify the nearest source-supported controlled value for that exact statement type. Do not infer Grade by locating an older occurrence of the same Theme or Sub-Theme combination.
- Apply scope evidence in this order: a value explicit in the current target source; clear bounded same-page heading context that establishes a visual reading-order inversion; then the nearest recognized candidate for that exact scope type in source_context.scope_context_candidates or, when no recognized candidate is available, the first matching entry in source_context.section_path_recent_first.
- In this curriculum, Grade remains active across subsequent pages, tables, and organizer sections until another Grade heading supersedes it. A Grade is not stale merely because its page_index precedes the target page. A newer Theme or Sub-Theme supersedes older entries of that same type but does not supersede the active Grade.
- When a grade-opening page clearly places a Grade heading after the current Theme/Sub-Theme in DocumentIR order, use the bounded same-page layout evidence and correct a stale carried Grade. Do not treat every following heading as governing.
- Reject a draft identity-scope value when it skips a nearer recognized value for the same scope dimension and relies on an older value without explicit target evidence, clear bounded same-page evidence, or an authoritative runtime rule supporting the override.
- Verify every scope explanation and extraction note against the actual compact payload. A draft that cites an absent page, heading, same-page context record, direction, source text, or scope candidate contains a material factual error. Set passed=false and return a corrected result.
- Source-context headings and scope candidates remain context-only. Do not create, quote, or anchor a candidate from them.
- Repeated Grade, Theme, and Sub-Theme headings on later pages are still valid extractions for their own visible windows. Do not remove them merely because the same organizer appears elsewhere; global deduplication occurs later.
- Treat the local page heading pair as authoritative when it clearly establishes a visual inversion. Preserve visible variants such as SUBTHEME, Primary Measure or Primary Measures, Secondary Measure or Secondary Measures, and PRIMARY: THREE without correcting their spelling, spacing, capitalization, or punctuation.

TOPIC VALIDATION
- Each visible Topic cell names one Topic grouping SFI for that source row. Preserve the complete visible Topic cell in description and source_text, including the leading Arabic ordinal and punctuation, such as 1., 2., or 4. The ordinal is not an official statement code and must never be placed in statement_code. It is source-facing occurrence material needed to distinguish repeated labels such as 1. Addition and 3. Addition within the same Grade, Theme, and Sub-Theme.
- Retain semantic numbers that are part of the topic label, such as Whole numbers 1-5, Whole number 0 (Zero), Whole numbers 6-9, Whole number 10, Whole Numbers 1-99, Whole numbers 1-200, Whole numbers up to 999, and Length II.
- Identical or near-identical topic labels may represent distinct source rows and must not be collapsed within a window solely because the wording matches. In particular, Primary One contains separate Addition and Subtraction topic rows for general operations and later for missing-number work; repeated labels across grades are also distinct. Accept multiple same-text Topic candidates when they cite different visible rows and each row has its own objectives or content.
- Lexically identical labels at different hierarchy levels are separate SFIs when visibly present. BASIC OPERATIONS may be both Theme and Sub-Theme, and Open Sentences may be both Sub-Theme and Topic. Do not delete one as a duplicate or force them to share a statement_type.
- Do not reject a source-visible topic because its placement seems semantically surprising, such as Fractions under the visible Whole Number sub-theme. Extraction must follow the source, not repair the curriculum hierarchy.

PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVE VALIDATION
- Extract exactly one Performance Objective candidate for each top-level objective in a Performance Objectives cell. Usually these are Arabic-numbered items. Do not combine an entire multi-item objective cell into one candidate, and do not split one top-level objective into smaller skills or phrases.
- A shared visible stem such as Pupils should be able to:, Pupil should be able to:, The pupils should be able to:, or The pupil should be able to: semantically scopes every top-level objective in the same Performance Objectives cell. When the stem is needed to make an objective a complete normative statement, candidate description should contain the exact visible stem followed by the exact visible wording of that objective. Do not invent a stem when the source row does not show one or when the objective is already a complete standalone statement.
- Apply the shared-stem source-evidence rule carefully. For the first objective, source_text may contain the stem plus the objective when they are contiguous in the source. For later objectives, or whenever earlier peer objectives intervene, source_text should contain only the exact contiguous current objective item. Do not require source_text to repeat the noncontiguous shared stem, do not include earlier peer objectives merely to make the stem contiguous, and do not treat the resulting description/source_text difference as an error. It is valid for description to combine the exact visible stem and exact visible objective from the same cited table row while source_text remains the contiguous objective excerpt.
- Preserve subordinate complements inside their parent objective. For example, bullets such as Home and School under one time objective, or listed mathematical relationships under one objective, are not separate Performance Objective SFIs.
- Source numbering is often irregular, duplicated, or skipped. Preserve the visible objective wording and any materially included source numbering; do not infer missing objectives, renumber source items, repair grammar, or correct mathematical or typographical errors. Candidate IDs must still follow the output contract, but source list numbers are not statement codes.

CONTENT COLUMN POLICY
- Content cells are official curriculum elaboration and may help interpret the Topic and Performance Objectives in the same row, but they are not SFI nodes in this v0 graph.
- Do not emit Content candidates, even when a Content cell contains a concise concept, skill phrase, Roman-numeral list, formula, or apparent learning statement.
- Do not copy Content wording into a Performance Objective description, source_text, or source anchor unless that wording is independently visible in the Performance Objectives cell.
- Content list markers, examples, properties, object lists, values, and formulas are contextual evidence only and are never statement_code.

CRITICAL EXCLUSIONS AND COMMON FALSE POSITIVES
- Teacher Activities and Pupils Activities contain instructional procedures, pupil tasks, games, worked examples, classroom demonstrations, and real-life applications. They are not SFIs.
- Evaluation Guide cells frequently begin with Pupils to: and closely resemble Performance Objectives. They are assessment prompts and must not be extracted as SFIs.
- Teaching and Learning Resources or Materials are not SFIs, including counters, charts, coins, rulers, shapes, cards, containers, clocks, and other listed objects.
- Do not extract arithmetic expressions, sample calculations, missing-number boxes, tables of factors or multiples, monetary denominations, dates, days, units, examples beginning with e.g., or classroom scenarios as standalone SFIs merely because they are prominent.
- Repeated table headers and retained continuation headers are not SFIs. A header-only table window should normally contain no SFI candidates.
- Do not create LearningComponents, relationships, inferred parent nodes, or synthesized mathematical skills beyond the visible Topic and top-level Performance Objective items.

SOURCE FIDELITY AND DOCUMENT ANOMALIES
- This curriculum is English-only. Candidate language should be en unless the actual supporting source units indicate otherwise. Do not translate or modernize wording.
- Preserve source-visible spelling, grammar, capitalization, punctuation, mathematical notation, and apparent mistakes. Do not silently repair phrases, duplicated numbering, skipped numbering, inconsistent singular or plural forms, old Nigerian currency notation, incorrect-looking arithmetic, or OCR-visible punctuation.
- Preserve mathematical symbols as exposed in the compact source window, including fractions such as ½, ¼, ¾ or slash forms such as 1/2 and 1/4, < and >, x or multiplication-sign variants, division-sign variants, N or ₦ variants, k denominations, and H.T.U. Do not invent a missing box, symbol, number, or word that is not present in the compact source.
- description and source_text must be grounded only in the current visible block, raw header, or raw source row. Do not quote section_path, preceding or following same-page heading context, canonical headers, filldown helper cells, or neighboring columns as candidate evidence. If a Topic or other label appears only in filldown_context_rows, use it only to understand the row scope and do not emit a new candidate from that helper-only text.
- For a table candidate, verify that its cited table_row_indexes or table_header_indexes actually contain the candidate wording and that the candidate is assigned the source role of that cited column. Do not allow a valid quote from an excluded column to masquerade as a Performance Objective candidate.
- Adjacent extraction windows may overlap and may legitimately repeat candidates from the same source row. Do not suppress a valid current-window candidate because it may also appear in another window; later registry and dedup stages handle cross-window duplicates.

NO-CODE POLICY
- This PDF contains no stable official alphanumeric SFI codes. statement_code should be null for every Grade, Theme, Sub-Theme, Topic, and Performance Objective candidate.
- Topic ordinals, objective numbers, Roman numerals, bullets, page numbers, row numbers, mathematical values, fractions, currency values, dates, units, arithmetic expressions, and example labels are never statement_code.

MATERIAL-CORRECTION STANDARD
- Mark the draft failed and return a complete corrected result when it omits a visible required Grade, Theme, Sub-Theme, Topic, or top-level Performance Objective; shortens a visible Theme or Sub-Theme heading by removing THEME, SUB-THEME, SUBTHEME, or its source-visible punctuation; extracts Content or any other excluded column or example as an SFI; combines or splits items at the wrong list level; assigns the wrong statement_type; invents source text; uses stale section context as evidence; keeps a stale prior Grade scope when clearer same-page heading context governs the visible Theme/Sub-Theme; skips the nearest recognized value for the same identity-scope statement type without source-supported override evidence; cites context not present in the supplied compact source window; or creates a non-null statement_code.
- Do not fail solely for harmless inclusion or omission of a visible list marker in description or source_text when the complete item wording, source role, ordering, and source references remain exact and unambiguous. Focus corrections on material semantic and source-grounding errors.
as.sfi_has_child_instructions: Resolve Nigeria Primary 1-3 Mathematics hasChild relationships conservatively. Use finalized SFIs only, and choose direct parents only from the supplied parent_candidates. The expected source hierarchy is StandardsFramework -> Grade -> Theme -> Sub-Theme -> Topic -> Performance Objective. Grade SFIs such as PRIMARY ONE, PRIMARY TWO, PRIMARY THREE, and source/OCR punctuation variants such as PRIMARY: THREE should normally attach directly to the StandardsFramework root. Theme SFIs should attach to the correct Grade. Sub-Theme SFIs should attach to the correct Theme within the correct Grade. Topic SFIs should attach to the correct Sub-Theme within the correct Theme and Grade. Performance Objective SFIs should attach to the Topic row that contains the objective. Content cells are contextual curriculum elaboration, not finalized SFIs, and must not be treated as parent or child nodes. Because this curriculum has no stable SFI codes, do not choose parents by topic number, list number, roman numeral, page number, arithmetic example, or row ordinal. A preserved Topic ordinal may help distinguish two local Topic occurrences after Grade/Theme/Sub-Theme scope is established, but it must not override same-row, same-table, active local heading, or other direct source hierarchy evidence. Repeated labels such as Whole Numbers, Addition, Subtraction, Multiplication, Division, Open Sentences, Money, Length, Time, Weight, Capacity, Area, Fractions, Data Collection, Symmetry, Pictograms, Shapes, Primary Measures, Secondary Measure(s), and Basic Operations are not globally unique; use grade, semantic identity scope, source order, recent section-path labels, same source segment/window, table row/header context, and nearest local source scope to choose the correct scoped parent. Treat active_outline_stack_parent, matched_section_path_label, same table context, same source context key, same segment/window, and nearest preceding grouping as retrieval evidence, not automatic truth. Prefer the most direct source-local parent over a broad or repeated label from another grade, theme, or sub-theme. Select the StandardsFramework root only for top-level Grade items or when no supplied finalized SFI parent is source-supported. Choose exactly one direct parent per child unless the source explicitly supports multiple direct memberships; if no supplied parent is source-supported, set unresolved=true. Direct parent policy: only Grade attaches directly to the StandardsFramework root; Theme attaches to Grade; Sub-Theme attaches to Theme; Topic attaches to Sub-Theme; Performance Objective attaches to its source-row Topic. Treat page-header text where PRIMARY, THEME, and SUB-THEME are visually co-located as one local hierarchy even if OCR or reading order emits the grade after the theme. When source context is needed to distinguish repeated parent labels, resolve each scope dimension independently. Treat a Grade as active until a newer Grade heading supersedes it, even when the active Grade originates on a preceding page. Do not choose an older Grade or Grade-scoped parent merely because the same Theme or Sub-Theme wording appeared with it earlier in the document. Candidate identity_scope_values and the nearest source-supported scope evidence should normally agree; when they materially conflict and no supplied parent is defensible, return unresolved rather than forcing an edge.
as.sfi_has_child_validation_instructions: Independently audit every Nigeria Primary 1-3 Mathematics hasChild decision against the bounded request. The expected direct hierarchy is StandardsFramework -> Grade -> Theme -> Sub-Theme -> Topic -> Performance Objective. Only Grade is normally root-level; Theme must resolve to the correct Grade; Sub-Theme to the correct Theme within the correct Grade; Topic to the correct Sub-Theme within the correct Theme and Grade; and each Performance Objective to the Topic represented by its source table row. Use each child and parent candidate's finalized identity_scope_values and scope_comparison to distinguish repeated labels across grades and organizer scopes. A direct-parent value match without matching ancestor scope is not sufficient. Treat cumulative section_path_labels, source_context_labels, active outline evidence, nearby windows, and repeated page headers as fallible evidence rather than an asserted hierarchy stack. In particular, page layouts can visually co-locate PRIMARY, THEME, and SUB-THEME while OCR or reading order emits the Grade after the Theme; the checker must reconstruct the source-local hierarchy semantically rather than following raw source order blindly. Performance Objectives should normally share the same source row/table context as their Topic parent. Topic ordinals, list numbers, page numbers, arithmetic examples, and row ordinals are not globally unique identifiers and must not override finalized grade/theme/sub-theme scope. Reject cross-grade, cross-theme, or cross-sub-theme parent selections when another supplied candidate matches the complete finalized scope and source structure. Reject root fallback when a defensible supplied direct parent exists. Return unresolved only when the bounded evidence is materially conflicting or insufficient after applying the source hierarchy and scope rules. Choose exactly one direct parent per child unless the source explicitly supports multiple direct memberships.
